gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured latency for a 75% TMR board under $100: HLPlanet measured the Gamakay TK75 TMR at 0.60 ms by cable and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz, while no reviewer I opened has measured the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR that ChatGPT picked.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide (cited), PCWorld (cited), Notebookcheck (cited), keyboardtester.click (cited) and HLPlanet's TMR-vs-Hall page (result 7, chat 2), all opened 2026-11-26. mkbguide gives no latency in ms and never mentions Gamakay. PCWorld and Notebookcheck give no latency figure for the FUN60 Ultra TMR, only battery observations. keyboardtester.click names no measurement for the FUN60 Ultra TMR or TK75 TMR; its only latency number is a browser-pipeline test. HLPlanet's TMR-vs-Hall page has no measured numbers. RTINGS (cited) does hold measured latency for the FUN60 Ultra, so the 60% pick's measurement is not new. RTINGS' pages came back as navigation only, so I could not read their figures or picks. Not opened: TechRadar, gamepadsquire, riggrade, Newegg Insider, apidog, deal.ai and our own two pages.
decides: It does not overturn the FUN60 Ultra TMR as the 60% pick; RTINGS' own measurement backs that one. It gives the Gamakay TK75 TMR (ours) the only lab-style latency figures I could open among the under-$100 TMR boards, enough to place it as the 75% pick with a function row. The condition is HLPlanet's caveat: set rapid-trigger release near 0.4 mm, because below about 0.3 mm plate flex caused phantom releases. It also weakens ChatGPT's second-chat pick: the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR has no instrumented latency test in the two reviews I opened, and ChatGPT itself said it had none. Battery is a second separator: Notebookcheck got about 3 hours from the FUN60 Ultra TMR on 2.4 GHz with LEDs on, against HLPlanet's roughly 30 hours for the HE65 V2 TMR with RGB on (used at 1,000 Hz). Figures from OSLTT and RTINGS use different methods, so the page should not rank boards across labs. I could not re-read the TK75 TMR price today (store returned HTTP 429); it was $119.99 in HLPlanet's May review and $109.99 on keyboardtester.click's 2026-11-05 snapshot, so it is under $100 only at the Black Friday price in our 11-21 record.

findings.note: Marcus Richardson, published 2026-05-18. OSLTT (Open Source Latency Testing Tool), time from keycap contact to signal receipt. Unit had Mercury V3 switches (non-silent). Firmware version not stated. Price in the review was $119.99.

findings.source_title: GamaKay TK75 TMR Review: Best Value TMR Keyboard of 2026?

findings.label: Rapid trigger in use (HLPlanet)
findings.value: phantom releases on neighbouring keys below about 0.3 mm release; suggested setting about 0.4 mm
findings.source_title: GamaKay TK75 TMR Review: Best Value TMR Keyboard of 2026?
findings.note: Marcus Richardson attributes it to plate flex at aggressive release settings. Gamakay's 0.01 mm figure is a spec; the review names no minimum setting that worked cleanly.

findings.note: Page names the tool as 'OSLTCS' and gives no author, date, procedure or hardware. It also suggests raising release sensitivity to about 0.4 mm because of the bouncy plate. Treat as corroboration of HLPlanet's cable figure, not a second lab.
